Lagomplan look-and-feel audit

www.lagomplan.com, Spanish, desktop 1440 and mobile 390, captured 18 Nov 2026 against production (main commit eb90c3c). Read-only: nothing was changed. Canon = home, /guias and a guide page. Caveat: canon is not one thing: home and /guias disagree on H1 size, body colour and button shape, and guide pages use a third voice. Where canon splits I say so and recommend.

Top 5ScreenshotsElements side by sideInconsistency listCode origin & tokensMobile filtersRecommendations

Top 5 issues by visual impact

  1. Buttons: two families side by side size M
    Home, guide pages, planner and login use 8px rectangles (some in 11px mono caps, 41px tall); /guias, hub, hotels, landings and the guest guide use pills. A visitor going home → guides → hotels sees three different primary buttons.
  2. Headings: no shared page-title style size M
    H1 runs 40–76px, weight 400–900, pine / #1A1A1A / #0F1A16, tracking from 0 to -2.9px. Landings and smart-finds switch to serif; the planner's H2 is weight 400; hub section titles are 22px.
  3. Cards: radius 30 / 20 / 16, three border colours size L
    The hub and hotels use the catalog tokens (r20, pine@10% border, no shadow, 40px thumbnail); /guias uses r30 with a shadow and full-bleed art; guide pages and the guest guide use r16 with #E2DDD5. Side by side the product feels like three sites.
  4. Text colours and eyebrows: a green system and a grey system size M
    Body copy uses seven colours (#3E5F58, #3E5650, #4A4A4A at weight 300, #2D6B57, #7A7773, pine at 72%/80%). Eyebrows come in three voices (sage 11px, #4F6B64 13px bold, DM Mono). 145 hardcoded #E4DFD8 borders sit next to the --line-* tokens.
  5. Forms and filters: four chips, four inputs, two mobile filter patterns size M
    Chips run 24–50px tall; inputs are 2px-radius (home/planner), 8px (login), pill (landings). Mobile filters differ per page (/guias wraps with "+ Más", hub and hotels scroll sideways). Smart-finds/familias additionally renders in the browser's default fonts because it names "Manrope"/"Fraunces" directly, which the site never loads.

What I could not capture: "Mi Viaje" and "planner form" are the same page (/es/planificador); the real trip-result view needs a saved trip, so /es/ejemplos (the examples page) stands in; /es/mis-viajes shows the signed-out state. Screenshots are the first ≈1000px of each page (full pages are 1.2k–73k px tall); computed styles were read from the full DOM.

2–3. Shared elements side by side

canondrift Each caption shows the computed style read from the live page.

Eyebrow labels

Canon: Manrope 11/500, caps, tracking 1.32px, sage #6B8F86 (home, /guias, planner). Three other voices exist.

Recommendation Keep canon (sage 11/500). For the catalog pages this means dropping --label #4F6B64 13/700 for eyebrows. Contrast: sage #6B8F86 on cream is about 3.4:1, so use it at 12px/600 or darken sage slightly rather than bold the whole system. Size S. Mono eyebrows on landings/guest guide can stay as a deliberate editorial layer, but should be labelled "editorial" in the system.

H1

Canon is already two voices: home 60/700 (-1.5px) and /guias 72/800 (-2.88px) are both Manrope, pine, tight tracking; guide pages use Manrope 52/400 in near-black #1A1A1A.

Recommendation Define one page-title style: Manrope 800, pine, tracking -0.04em, sized by one clamp (≈ 44px mobile → 64px desktop), i.e. /guias without the 72px outlier. Keep the light 400 style only for guide pages if Elena wants the "editorial" feel, and then name it. Fix planner (#0F1A16 → pine), login/ejemplos (no tracking, 62px line-height on 40px), smart-finds/familias (900 weight, 76px). Size M (about 10 page headers; one shared PageTitle would cover it).

H2 / section titles

Canon: home 40/700, /guias 36/800 (-0.72px). Drift ranges from 22px to light-weight 400.

Recommendation Keep canon 36–40/700–800. The planner's 34px weight-400 H2 is the one that looks broken next to the rest. Catalog card titles are H2-tagged at 22px, which is a card title, not a section title, so mark them H3. Size S.

Body text

Seven different greens/greys for body copy across the site (canon alone has three: #3E5F58, pine @72%, #4A4A4A at weight 300).

Recommendation One body colour (--ink-2 #3E5650 is already the token the catalog uses and is within a shade of home's #3E5F58) at 15–16px/400. Retire #4A4A4A/300 weight (guide pages) and #7A7773 (smart-finds), which read grey against the green system. Size M because the guide pages hardcode it in about 60 places.

Search fields

Close already: same 56px pill. Only border and fill differ.

Recommendation Keep canon border (#C8BFB5) and fill (#FFFDF9), or move both to tokens; the visible difference is small. Size S.

Form inputs

Four different text-input styles: 2px-radius 13px (home and planner forms), 8px (login), pill 16px (landings), translucent 8px on dark (guest guide).

Recommendation Canon here is the weakest spot: 2px corners and 38px height on the home/planner form clash with every pill on the site and are under the 44px touch size. Recommend 48px height, 12px radius or pill (match the search field), border --line-chip. Border #C8D9D3 on the home form is the old brand "sage" and should go. Size M (planner form has about 400 hardcoded colour values).

Filter chips: default and selected

Four chip systems. /guias 42px/13/700 on sand; catalog 44px/15/600 on white; smart-finds 37px/12 grey; guest guide 34px with a mint selected state; home interest chips are 24px tall with 10px text.

Recommendation Use the catalog chip (44px, 15/600) everywhere: it is the only one that meets touch-target size and it already lives in components/catalog/Chip.tsx. Keep the pine fill for "selected" (reject mint). /guias is canon on paper but its 42px chip is a 2px miss, so it adopts the catalog chip rather than the other way round. Size M.

Tags / pills (non-interactive)

Four styles; smart-finds uses an off-palette teal (#E1F5EE on #085041) that exists nowhere else.

Recommendation Keep canon: 11/500 on sand with a warm border. The hub's 13/600 borderless pill is heavier than the card title hierarchy supports. Size S.

Cards

Radius 30 (/guias) · 20 (catalog tokens) · 16 (guide hotel cards, guest guide, landings). Border colours differ (#C8BFB5, #E2DDD5, pine @10%); only /guias and the guest guide have shadows. Image treatment differs: /guias full-bleed illustration; hub and hotels a 40px thumbnail beside text; guide hotel cards no image.

Recommendation Two card families are legitimate (large destination card with image; compact information card). Define them once: destination card r24 + border #E4DFD8-equivalent token + soft shadow (/guias, home, guide previews), info card r16 + same border, no shadow (hub, hotels, guide hotels, guest guide, landings). That moves hub/hotels from r20 to r16 and /guias from r30 to r24. Size L (touches the most files; pays back in every later page).

Primary buttons

Canon contains both families: home and guide pages use 8px-radius rectangles (home Manrope 12/600 with 1.5px tracking; guide pages DM Mono 11 caps); /guias uses a pill. Newer pages (hub, hotels, landings, guest guide) all use pills.

Recommendation This needs Elena's call because canon disagrees with itself. My recommendation: pill, Manrope 14–15/700, 48px high, no mono caps, no 1.5px tracking. Reasons: /guias (canon) already does it, 7 of 11 surfaces use it, and 11px caps buttons fail the 44px touch rule on mobile (login 41px). Keeping 8px rectangles would mean restyling the hub, hotels, landings and guest guide (4 surfaces) instead of home, guide pages, planner and login (4 surfaces); equal cost, worse touch targets. Size M.

Secondary buttons

Outline buttons: 8px on home, pill on hub/smart-finds/landings; the guide-page "Reservar" is a filled pine mono button (not outline).

Recommendation Follow the primary decision: pill outline, 1px --line-btn (pine @22%), same height as the primary. Size S once the primary is decided.

Header / nav

The site nav is identical (white, 100px, fixed) on 11 pages. Three pages deviate by design: the landings have no site nav, the guest guide has its own 88px cream blur header.

Recommendation Nothing to fix on the site nav. Decide whether landings should carry the site nav (acquisition pages often should not; keep). Size S (decision only).

Footer

Identical on all site pages (white, 48/24 padding). Landings use a bare 32px footer; the guest guide has none (partner-branded by design).

Recommendation Keep. Add the minimum legal links to landings if they lack them (cookie settings / privacy) since they collect emails. Size S.

4. Where the drift comes from, and token problems

Three code lineages produce the drift:

  • Catalog system (components/catalog: PageHeader, FilterPanel, Chip, CatalogCard, ResultsBar + the --ink-2/--label/--line-*/--radius-* tokens). Used by /experiencias and /hoteles only (ExperiencesHub, HotelsClient). It is internally consistent (the hub and hotels pages match each other to the pixel) and token-driven (only 10 hex literals in the folder), but it picked its own values: r20 cards, 13/700 eyebrows, 15/600 chips, 22px section titles, pine@10% borders.
  • Original components (components/guides, components/forms, the planner, home): hand-styled with Tailwind arbitrary values and inline styles, about 800 hex literals, the stale brand colours, mono-caps buttons. This is where the 8px buttons, the 2px inputs and the grey neutrals come from.
  • Own-CSS surfaces: smart-finds (inline styles, off-palette teal, fonts named literally), the guest guide (guia.module.css), the two landings (editorial.module.css, Fraunces override). Each is a separate mini design system.

So the answer to "does the drift come from the catalog system?" is: partly. The catalog pages are the newest and most disciplined, but they diverge from canon because they were built to their own tokens instead of the original pages\' values. The larger source of inconsistency is the original components, which never had tokens at all, and the three own-CSS surfaces.

Token issueDetail
Same value, several names--pine = --forest = --ink #0F3A33; --coral = --accent #E1615B; --cream = --card #FFF9F3. Marked "migration aliases, remove after component color pass" in globals.css; the pass never happened.
Defined twiceThe six brand colours exist in tailwind.config.js as hex literals and again in :root in globals.css. Changing one does not change the other.
Tokens nobody usesThe type scale --text-xs … --text-3xl has 0 references in app/ and components/. Pages size type with arbitrary Tailwind values (text-[13px]) and inline styles.
Hardcoded instead of tokens199 distinct hex literals in app/ and components/. #0F3A33 appears 438 times (should be var(--pine)); neutrals: #E4DFD8 ×145, #7A7A76 ×96, #B8B5AF ×73, #1C1C1A ×61, #E2DDD5 ×37, #D8CFC1 ×40, #CEC8C0 ×32; near-pine #1F3D37 ×50. components/guides holds 385 hex values, the planner 399.
Two border systemsCatalog: --line-card/panel/chip/btn (pine at 12/14/18/22%), used 11 times. Original: --border #C8BFB5 (29 uses) plus hardcoded #E4DFD8 / #E2DDD5 / #D8CFC1 / #CEC8C0. Same job, six neutrals.
Text colour tokens divergeCatalog --ink-2 #3E5650 and --label #4F6B64; alias --muted #3D6B5C; home body #3E5F58; planner #2D6B57; guides #4A4A4A / #7A7A76; sage #6B8F86 used as eyebrow on canon pages. Five greens for secondary text.
Radius tokens cover two values--radius-card 20 and --radius-panel 24 are used only by the catalog. Original components use 30, 28, 18, 16, 12, 10, 8, 3, 2 px literals; the guest guide has its own --radius-xl 16.
Stale brand colours still shipping#1B4D3E (old "forest") ×44 (17 in the home HeroForm, plus my-trips), #C8D9D3 (old sage) ×24, #F4F0E8 (old sand) ×33. The brand note at the top of globals.css lists them as corrected, but the components never moved.
A parallel token setapp/guia has its own variables (--paper, --sage-soft #A9C3BB, --radius-xl, --shadow-card; 226 var() uses); landings have editorial.module.css overriding the heading rule with Fraunces. Both are deliberate, neither is documented as a variant of the system.

6. Mobile filter pattern: /guias vs hub

Measured. /guias: one facet (13 style chips), wrapping rows, 6 shown plus "+ Más" that expands inline. Hub: search + 3 labelled rows (Región 7, Para quién 4, Tipo 6), each scrolls sideways; at 390×844 the first result line sits at y≈680, about half of each row is off-screen, and there is no clear-all control. Hoteles: 2 sideways rows. Hub and Hoteles share components/catalog/FilterPanel (its header documents the sideways rows as intentional); /guias has its own implementation in GuidesClient.tsx. I found no bottom-sheet filter design in the repo; the only bottom sheets are the (hidden) plan tray and the trip booking drawer.

Recommendation: one pattern, a bottom sheet. Search field plus a "Filtros (n)" button; active filters as removable chips under the search; the sheet holds every facet as wrapping chips with a live "Ver N resultados" button and "Limpiar". Desktop unchanged. Build it once in FilterPanel and move /guias onto it (single facet). It scales from /guias\' one facet to the hub\'s three or more, frees the first screen, fixes the 44px target, and retires both "+ Más" and the sideways rows. Risk: filters become one tap further away; mitigate with the count badge and active chips, and watch the experience_filter event rate before/after. Size M, reusing the existing booking-drawer sheet pattern.
